# Dialog

A window over the page that takes attention until people finish or close it.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Multi-brand</span></p>

## See it live

## When to use it

**In Multi-brand:** Change a plan.

- **Use it when:** People must decide or finish something before going back: a short form, an important choice.
- **Not when:** A short status (toast), extra detail on the page (accordion), or a side panel that should not block the page (sheet).

Instead:

- [Sheet](./sheet.md): A side panel; the page stays in view.
- [Toast](./toast.md): Does not interrupt.
- [Alert dialog](./alert-dialog.md): Confirms something that cannot be undone.

## How Multi-brand uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">A menu or dialog</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> elevation.overlay and a dimmed page</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> No shadow</div></div><div class="cap">Same overlay in every brand.</div></div></div>

## Words

- Shared structure: object, state, next step.
- Brand tone lives in headlines and marketing copy, not in errors.
- Errors and confirmations read the same in every brand.
- Use: Get started, Plan, Order. Avoid: Brand-specific words in errors, Jargon.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Get started

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

| Keyboard | What happens | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| undefined | Escape closes it. | undefined |
| undefined | Tab stays inside while it is open. | undefined |

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It is a dialog with a title; the page behind is hidden from screen readers. undefined
- [ ] Focus moves in when it opens and back to the trigger when it closes. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add dialog
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Dialog reads 4 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Dialog's tokens to change Dialog alone.
